subject: Civil Engineering
title: The Akashi Kaikyo Bridge
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Akashi Kaikyo Bridge.

hook.text: Japan's Akashi Kaikyo spans 6,532 feet — the world's longest suspension bridge.

buildup.text: It crosses a strait with 9-knot tidal currents, typhoons, and earthquake faults.

discovery.text: Tuned mass dampers in each tower reduce sway from wind and seismic forces.

twist.text: During construction, the 1995 Kobe earthquake shifted the towers one meter apart.

climax.text: Engineers adjusted the design mid-build to accommodate the new gap. It still works.

punchline.text: An earthquake moved the bridge — and engineers just adapted.

quiz.question: What happened to the Akashi Kaikyo Bridge during the 1995 Kobe earthquake?
options: Several cables snapped and had to be replaced
The towers shifted apart by about one meter, requiring design adjustments
The bridge collapsed and had to be entirely rebuilt
